lane_calls: The frame's Aramaic is the Aramaic of the texts the reader serves: Official/Biblical Aramaic (PanLex arc; Wiktionary lang «Aramaic» with code arc or arc-bib), Old Aramaic (oar), Jewish Babylonian Aramaic (tmr; Wiktionary «Jewish Babylonian Aramaic»), Jewish Palestinian Aramaic (jpa), Samaritan Aramaic (sam). Hebrew is any value whose name holds «Hebrew» (hbo-000, hbo-003, etc.). OUT: modern Neo-Aramaic of any community (aii Assyrian Neo-Aramaic, cld Chaldean Neo-Aramaic, Wiktionary «Lishana Deni» lsd), Classical Syriac (syc, including a Wiktionary item whose lang reads «Aramaic» but whose code is syc), Mandaic. A value outside the closed table stops the builder.

Each now admits only the rows whose own language field is Hebrew or the Aramaic of the texts the reader serves: 4070 rows, listed in send back v1.1 (landing-own-language-v1.1.jsonl). Assyrian Neo-Aramaic, Lishana Deni and Classical Syriac rows are out (the lane's call). Harkavy stays REFUSED and now carries the owner's own words of 1 and 6 September; the send back v1 sentence «The language ban of 31 August is repealed: language is judged at the word» was the lane's, not the owner's, and is withdrawn. The owner's words of 1 September let other languages appear inside works; they never let anything but Hebrew or Aramaic be an M.
